37/S0.subgoal: Explain the objective of ensuring usability in the final product of a system.

37/S1.subgoal: Introduce contextual inquiry and the Majuli VR Tour case study.

37/S2.subgoal: Compare and contrast how contextual inquiry outcomes can be used to create design guidelines or functional requirements.

37/S3.subgoal: Illustrate how observations from contextual inquiry can be framed into practical design guidelines.

37/S4.subgoal: Explain how usability requirements can be converted into functional requirements to facilitate code design.

37/S5.subgoal: Define functional requirements and explain their role in the Software Requirements Specification (SRS).

37/S6.subgoal: Describe the hierarchical structure used for formally specifying requirements in an SRS document.

37/S7.subgoal: Demonstrate how to convert general observations into structured functional requirements within an SRS using an example.

37/S8.subgoal: Summarize the utilization pathways of contextual inquiry results, whether as guidelines or functional requirements.

37/S9.subgoal: Identify and describe the specific user groups for the Majuli VR Tour based on field observations.

37/S10.subgoal: Address the key design challenge of cyber sickness and managing large data coverage in the VR tour context.

37/S11.subgoal: Identify other crucial usability challenges for the VR tour, such as location awareness and combining heritage experiences.

37/S12.subgoal: Summarize the scope of the lecture, covering requirements gathering methods, analysis, and practical application.

37/S13.subgoal: Outline how the identified usability issues will be addressed in the subsequent lecture on system design.
